sets.title: Table: Quarterly sales of five products of a Trichy snack unit (₹ lakh). Each Total is the sum of the four quarters and the last row gives column totals. Cells marked — are not given.
Table: Monthly rainfall recorded at five stations in a quarter (mm). Each Total is the sum of the three months and the last row gives column totals. Cells marked — are not given.
Table: Goods wagons loaded at five railway yards in four weeks. Each Total is the sum of the four weeks and the last row gives column totals. Cells marked — are not given.
Table: Candidates in five coaching centres. Boys % is the percentage of boys among the Total; Boys and Girls are numbers. Cells marked — are not given.
Table: Staff in five footwear plants. Men % is the percentage of men among the Total; Men and Women are numbers. Cells marked — are not given.
Table: Registered voters in five assembly constituencies. Male % is the percentage of male voters among the Total; Male and Female are numbers (in hundreds). Cells marked — are not given.

questions.questionText: What was the average value per product in Q1? (in ₹ lakh, correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: The column total for Q1 is 100, so the blank does not matter. Average = 100 ÷ 5 = 20.0.
questions.shortcut: Use the Total row of the column; no need to fill the blank.

questions.questionText: What is the missing value for Peanut chikki in Q2? (₹ lakh)
questions.explanation: Row total = 84. Known cells add to 62. Missing = 84 − 62 = 22.
questions.shortcut: Row total minus the known cells in the row.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of all the 4 missing values in the table? (₹ lakh)
questions.explanation: Missing values: Banana chips / Q3 = 28, Murukku / Q4 = 18, Varkey / Q1 = 30, Peanut chikki / Q2 = 22. Sum = 98.
questions.shortcut: Fill each blank from its row total, then add.

questions.questionText: The missing value for Murukku in Q4 is what percentage of Murukku's Total? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: Find the blank first, and divide by that row's own Total.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the missing value for Banana chips in Q3 more than the missing value for Peanut chikki in Q2? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: First blank = 28; second blank = 22 (each from its row total). Percentage more = (28−22) ÷ 22 × 100 = 27.3%.
questions.shortcut: Base is the quantity after 'than'.

questions.questionText: What is the missing value for Kodaikanal in August? (mm)
questions.explanation: Row total = 360. Known cells add to 235. Missing = 360 − 235 = 125.
questions.shortcut: Row total minus the known cells in the row.

questions.questionText: What was the average value per station in August? (in mm, correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: The column total for August is 540, so the blank does not matter. Average = 540 ÷ 5 = 108.0.
questions.shortcut: Use the Total row of the column; no need to fill the blank.

questions.questionText: The missing value for Ooty in September is what percentage of Ooty's Total? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: Find the blank first, and divide by that row's own Total.

questions.questionText: Which station had the highest value in July?
questions.explanation: After filling the blank, July values are Coimbatore 60, Ooty 120, Madurai 40, Chennai 90, Kodaikanal 100. Highest is Ooty.
questions.shortcut: The blank may itself be the highest; do not skip it.

questions.questionText: Which station showed the highest percentage increase from July to September?
questions.explanation: After filling blanks, % increase: Coimbatore 50.0%, Ooty -8.3%, Madurai 75.0%, Chennai 66.7%, Kodaikanal 35.0%. Highest is Madurai.
questions.shortcut: Fill every blank in the two columns that matter before comparing growth rates.

questions.questionText: What was the average value per yard in Week 4? (in wagons, correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: The column total for Week 4 is 760, so the blank does not matter. Average = 760 ÷ 5 = 152.0.
questions.shortcut: Use the Total row of the column; no need to fill the blank.

questions.questionText: What is the missing value for Arakkonam in Week 2? (wagons)
questions.explanation: Row total = 840. Known cells add to 660. Missing = 840 − 660 = 180.
questions.shortcut: Row total minus the known cells in the row.

questions.questionText: Which yard had the highest value in Week 3?
questions.explanation: After filling the blank, Week 3 values are Jolarpet 120, Erode 100, Arakkonam 220, Tondiarpet 90, Podanur 150. Highest is Arakkonam.
questions.shortcut: The blank may itself be the highest; do not skip it.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of all the 4 missing values in the table? (wagons)
questions.explanation: Missing values: Jolarpet / Week 4 = 180, Arakkonam / Week 2 = 180, Tondiarpet / Week 3 = 90, Podanur / Week 1 = 110. Sum = 560.
questions.shortcut: Fill each blank from its row total, then add.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the missing value for Jolarpet in Week 4 more than the missing value for Podanur in Week 1? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: First blank = 180; second blank = 110 (each from its row total). Percentage more = (180−110) ÷ 110 × 100 = 63.6%.
questions.shortcut: Base is the quantity after 'than'.

questions.questionText: What is the number of girls for Gandhipuram?
questions.explanation: In the row of Gandhipuram, use Total = Boys + Girls and Boys % = Boys ÷ Total × 100 on the two known figures. Completed row: Total 300, Boys % 40, Boys 120, Girls 180. The asked figure is 180.
questions.shortcut: Any two of the four figures in a row fix the other two.

questions.questionText: Overall, what percentage of all candidates are boys? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Total boys = 850; grand total = 1800. Percentage = 47.2%. (A simple average of the five percentages would be wrong.)
questions.shortcut: Add the numbers, not the percentages.

questions.questionText: What is the total number of girls across all five centres?
questions.shortcut: Complete each row first; then add the column.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between the largest and the smallest Total among the five centres?
questions.shortcut: Find every Total first.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the number of girls in Tambaram more than that in Gandhipuram? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Girls in Tambaram = 250; in Gandhipuram = 180. More by (250−180) ÷ 180 × 100 = 38.9%.
questions.shortcut: Fill both rows' blanks first; base is the second entity.

questions.questionText: What is the total number of candidates in all five plants together?
questions.explanation: Totals after filling blanks: 600, 450, 800, 500, 360. Sum = 2710.
questions.shortcut: Recover every blank Total before adding.

questions.questionText: In which plant is the percentage of men the highest?
questions.explanation: Men % after filling: Plant A 70%, Plant B 60%, Plant C 50%, Plant D 80%, Plant E 25%. Highest is Plant D.
questions.shortcut: Recover the blank percentages from the counts.

questions.questionText: Overall, what percentage of all candidates are men? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Total men = 1580; grand total = 2710. Percentage = 58.3%. (A simple average of the five percentages would be wrong.)
questions.shortcut: Add the numbers, not the percentages.

questions.questionText: What is the total number of women across all five plants?
questions.shortcut: Complete each row first; then add the column.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the number of women in Plant C more than that in Plant A? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Women in Plant C = 400; in Plant A = 180. More by (400−180) ÷ 180 × 100 = 122.2%.
questions.shortcut: Fill both rows' blanks first; base is the second entity.

questions.questionText: What is the number of male for Constituency 5?
questions.explanation: In the row of Constituency 5, use Total = Male + Female and Male % = Male ÷ Total × 100 on the two known figures. Completed row: Total 700, Male % 50, Male 350, Female 350. The asked figure is 350.
questions.shortcut: Any two of the four figures in a row fix the other two.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between the largest and the smallest Total among the five constituencys?
questions.shortcut: Find every Total first.

questions.questionText: In which constituency is the percentage of male the highest?
questions.explanation: Male % after filling: Constituency 1 45%, Constituency 2 55%, Constituency 3 60%, Constituency 4 40%, Constituency 5 50%. Highest is Constituency 3.
questions.shortcut: Recover the blank percentages from the counts.

questions.questionText: Overall, what percentage of all candidates are male? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Total male = 1700; grand total = 3500. Percentage = 48.6%. (A simple average of the five percentages would be wrong.)
questions.shortcut: Add the numbers, not the percentages.

questions.questionText: By what percentage is the number of female in Constituency 4 more than that in Constituency 5? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.explanation: Female in Constituency 4 = 540; in Constituency 5 = 350. More by (540−350) ÷ 350 × 100 = 54.3%.
questions.shortcut: Fill both rows' blanks first; base is the second entity.
